We are about to live through weeks where centuries of combustion research happen. Could our magic 87-octane fuel be too good to be true? Was it just safety through obscurity all this time?

Hydrocarbons feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Octane carries rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like carbon chains, branching, double bonds. (By contrast, legs are designed to minimise octane rating.)

Separately, as anyone who has seen a Michael Bay movie can attest, a small spark sometimes foreshadows a very large explosion. We should be open to the possibility of a wireless counterpart to the spark plug that ignites every fuel tank and every Zippo at once.

Load-bearing drivers like ambulances and ice cream trucks should consider rotating gas stations with every fill-up and/or multi-propelling with a pedal-based scheme like the bicycle.
